scenario: [LTIM.2.4.1]: a `where` that resolves a zone other than `UTC` is time-dependent, because its answer moves as the host asserts, replaces or retracts `TimeZoneOffset` facts ([LTIM.10.6]) with no change to the matched facts. So it is re-driven by the tick like a clock read, and a `logical` fact it justifies follows the zone's rows ([LLOG.3.11.1]). One `Europe/Paris` row covers the Event's instant, 2024-03-01T09:00Z, and the host replaces it twice under its key (`zone`, `valid_from`), changing only `offset_s`. Pump 1: offset 0, so the local hour is 9 and `open`'s `where` (`hour == 10`) is false; `closed` fires on `no Open`. Pump 2: offset 3600, hour 10, so `open` fires, `Open` is emitted, and `saw_open` fires. Pump 3: offset 7200, hour 11, so the match ends, `Open` is retracted, and `closed` fires again on the recreated `no Open` token. So the messages are exactly ['closed', 'open', 'closed']. The Event never changes after pump 1, and no rule matches `TimeZoneOffset`, so only the tick can carry the row changes into `open`. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete`'s `now_reeval_plan` through `dsc.typecheck.ltim_2_4_1_zone_read`, which moves the `where` into the terminal's fire guard behind the `$ClockTick` re-driver, read under each pump against the zone index (libds `ds_rete_tz_resolve`, Mercury `ds.eval.ltim_10_7_resolve`).
rules_ds:
use default

schema Event scope logical:
    id: Int key
    seen: Time mutable

schema Open scope logical:
    id: Int key

rule open:
    Event e where e.seen.local("Europe/Paris").hour == 10
->
    emit Open logical id: e.id

rule saw_open:
    Open
->
    log critical "open"

rule closed:
    Event e
    no Open o where o.id == e.id
->
    log critical "closed"
